I came here today to share with you a neat trick I learned from an old martial arts instructor of mine, which solves a tricky problem that I consider to be a fairly important one among practitioners of BWF, although most of them probably never even think about it. That trick, as stated in the title, is how to find what shoulder width for you is.

It sounds so simple, right? Surely everyone knows exactly what their shoulder width is? Actually, no. The very reason I know this trick is because I, like a lot of you I'm guessing, thought my shoulder width was way wider than it was when I was younger. I guess in my silly teenage mind I thought I looked like Dorian Yates and my shoulders were barn-door wide. My MA instructor caught this when I was doing some "shoulder width" pushups with an absurdly wide grip and shared with me this simple trick- simply raise your hands directly in front of you when standing or kneeling and look at them. That's your shoulder width.

I think shoulder width delusion and inaccuracy is a pretty big problem in the world of BWF and even weightlifting. Contributing to this is the fact that so many machines and pullup bars have a set "shoulder" width [don't buy these]. People's shoulder widths are DIFFERENT. My shoulder width is different from a small woman's shoulder width and Dorian Yate's shoulder width is different than mine. Anyways, I hope this post has helped you out and you will no longer suffer from any confusions/delusions as to what shoulder width is for you.

TL;DR I'm [probably going to be] the new mod of this sub. I'm a good guy. To find your shoulder width, raise your hands directly in front of you from standing or kneeling and look at them to see your shoulder width. It seems silly but a lot of people have this wrong for various reasons and knowing this trick will really help you out if you're one of them.
